name: skill-import
description: Use Anthropic SKILL.md files as Covia skills — in place from a file root or DLFS drive, or imported into a skillset. Load to bring SKILL.md files in.

content.inline:
## SKILL.md files as skills
An Anthropic Agent Skills file (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body) needs no conversion: frontmatter name and description are its index line, tools/skills/skillsets fill an empty facet, and other keys are ignored.

Use it where it is:
- `file://<root>/<dir>/SKILL.md` or `dlfs/<drive>/<path>` is a valid skill ref: a config.skills entry, the value of `w/skills/<name>`, or a direct load ref. The body is live, and the index re-reads the file every turn.

Import it — one file per call, never a directory; name each SKILL.md:
- The skill-import operation takes `{source, skillset?, content?}` and writes `<skillset>/<name>` (default `w/skills`; the name is the frontmatter's). It returns `{path, existed, ignored?}`, and the body never passes through your context. Re-importing overwrites.
- `content: "inline"` (default) copies the body; `"ref"` keeps it live in the file, with name and description as a snapshot — re-import when they change.
- `ignored` lists frontmatter keys with no Covia meaning (allowed-tools, argument-hint, metadata); license and compatibility are kept. Tool names from other harnesses are not operations: declare `skill.tools` yourself if the skill needs any.
- Supporting files (references/, scripts/, assets/) are not copied, so relative links in the body will not resolve. Bind what an agent needs as `skill.context` entries with `file://` refs, or use the file in place.

Translate without storing:
- The skill-parse operation takes the same `source`, or `text` already in hand, and returns `{metadata, ignored?}` — review it, then write it to `w/skills/<name>` with the lattice write operation or store it as an immutable asset.
